definition: VITAL (Validating Investment Tool for Advancing Life Sciences) was a Board Management Software machine learning proprietary software developed by Aging Analytics, a company registered in Bristol (England) and dissolved in 2017.
details: Andrew Garazha (the firm's Senior Analyst) declared that the project aimed "through iterative releases and updates to create a piece of software capable of making autonomous investment decisions." According to Nick Dyer-Witheford, VITAL 1.0 was a "basic algorithm". On 13 May 2014, Deep Knowledge Ventures, a Hong Kong venture capital firm, claimed to have appointed VITAL to its board of directors in order to prove that artificial intelligence could be an instrument for investment decision-making. The announcement received great press coverage despite the fact commentators consider this a publicity stunt. Fortune reported in 2019 that VITAL is no longer used.

explainer.lead: VITAL (Validating Investment Tool for Advancing Life Sciences) was proprietary machine learning software developed by Aging Analytics, a company registered in Bristol and dissolved in 2017. It was presented as a tool for making investment decisions.

tiers.eli5: A company said it put a computer program on its board of directors to help pick investments.
tiers.practitioner: Its senior analyst said the project aimed, through iterative releases and updates, at software capable of making autonomous investment decisions; by one account VITAL 1.0 was a basic algorithm, a pitfall of overstating what early systems can do.
tiers.paperLevel: Described as a Board Management Software machine learning proprietary tool; the public claims around its board appointment are not matched by detailed technical disclosure.
